page: The Vultr vhf-1c-2gb is an entry-level virtual machine within the High Frequency Compute product tier, built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides a single shared Intel virtual core running at 2.0 GHz, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB RAM, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. Local persistent storage includes an integrated 64 GB NVMe solid-state drive, and each instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the constrained single-core shared execution model. Synthetic CPU testing via stress-ng registers 1,266.88 for both single-threaded and multi-threaded runs, situating raw compute capacity in the lower quartile of tracked systems. PassMark CPU scoring yields 2,017.05 points, with an encryption subscore of 638.11 and database operations reaching 902.14 operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 100.1 GB/sec on cached 16 KB blocks but drops to 11.09 GB/sec read and 10.16 GB/sec write on larger uncached 256 MB arrays. Despite baseline limitations, the instance displays average throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 24.19 GB/sec, alongside Redis set operations handling 1.77 million transactions per second and static web throughput of 1.68 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a single shared core and 2.0 GB of RAM makes the vhf-1c-2gb a budget-friendly option for low-intensity cloud services where high sustained multi-threading is unnecessary. Tradeoffs involve potential resource contention typical of shared CPU configurations and limited headroom for memory-dense datasets. Consequently, this server instance is best fitted for lightweight web services, DNS or proxy hosting, microservices, minimal development environments, and baseline background utility tasks.
description: The Vultr vhf-1c-2gb is an entry-tier virtual server from the High Frequency Compute lineup, configured with a single shared Intel x86_64 virtual CPU operating at 2.0 GHz, 2.0 GB of system memory, and a local 64 GB NVMe SSD. It features essential hardware flags including AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2, but lacks hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark data demonstrates entry-level performance, reporting a stress-ng score of 1,266.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 2,017.05. Memory operations exhibit 100.1 GB/sec under small cached blocks and approximately 11.09 GB/sec under uncached read conditions. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches a competitive 24.19 GB/sec, while Redis handles 1.77 million set operations per second. Due to its shared core profile and 2.0 GB memory footprint, the vhf-1c-2gb delivers an economical footprint suited for static web serving, low-traffic network services, lightweight proxies, and low-complexity software development testing.
